root_cause_criterion.criterion: Before `Classifier_read()` may treat the suffix as NUL-terminated and continue to allocation/copy, it must establish `len != 128 + 1` immediately after the suffix scan so a completely filled 129-byte temporary buffer is rejected as corrupt chunk data.
root_cause_criterion.description: The vulnerable original reaches the protected `memcpy` even though the full-buffer rejection is false at the root site (`len_before_guard=129`, `suffix_capacity=129`). The authoritative fixed original is guarded on the stock PoC, and the closest source-grounded witness `third_rule_suffix_128_boundary` executes the same protected copy with the predicate true (`128 != 129`) and exits cleanly.

nodes.description: At `memcpy (mem, suffix, len)`, the vulnerable original uses `len=130` against the 129-byte stack array `suffix`, so the copy reads past the end of the source buffer.
nodes.evidence: The vulnerable original assertion trace records `classifier_memcpy.copy_len=130 > classifier_memcpy.suffix_capacity=129`.

edges.relation: The incremented suffix length produced at the root site is passed unchanged into the sink `memcpy` as its copy size, so the sink sees the same 130-byte count created by the off-by-one update.
edges.evidence: The vulnerable original trace records `classifier_root.copy_len_after_increment == classifier_memcpy.copy_len == 130`, and the fixed boundary witness preserves the same equality at 129 when the protected copy genuinely executes.

edges.relation: The same local stack buffer `suffix` observed at the root site is the source pointer passed into `memcpy`, so the oversized copy overreads that exact 129-byte array rather than a different object.
edges.evidence: The vulnerable original trace records `classifier_root.suffix_buffer == classifier_memcpy.suffix_buffer`, and the fixed boundary witness preserves the same pointer equality when the protected copy executes safely.
